sections.label: Masjid Al-Firdaus closure and mosque ratio

sentences.text: Does the Government have a target mosque-to-Muslim-resident population ratio, and if so, may we have some clarity on it?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This represents merely 0.1% of Muslims over 60 years old, and an even smaller fraction of our entire Muslim population.

sections.label: Disclosure of Fund assets
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will commit to full disclosure of the Fund's assets and regular updates to contributors' estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, will the Ministry commit to full disclosure of the assets managed under the Fund and to provide regular updates to the estates of contributors once the Fund becomes active?

sections.label: Expanding mental health services for couples
sections.summary: Asks whether there are plans to expand services, especially mental health and wellness support for young couples.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Are there plans to expand services, especially in mental health and wellness support for young couples?

sections.label: MENDAKI funds community of excellence
sections.summary: A request is made for the Ministry to consider allowing MENDAKI funds to establish a community of excellence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Chairman, I would like to request that the Ministry consider allowing MENDAKI funds be used to establish a community of excellence.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim literacy and youth jobs
sections.summary: It asks how literacy, numeracy and digital confidence efforts are assessed and how youth programmes align with growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, how do we assess the effectiveness of efforts to strengthen foundations in literacy, numeracy and digital confidence – especially for Malay/Muslim children who may lack learning support at home?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Second, how are programmes for Malay/Muslim youths aligned more closely with growth sectors – such as applied technology, advanced manufacturing and digital services – so that their participation truly opens pathways to good jobs?

sections.label: Seniors befriending and caregiver support
sections.summary: It asks how befriending programmes keep seniors connected and how caregivers in the sandwich generation can be supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, how are we strengthening befriending programmes for seniors, peer support and community touchpoints so that seniors remain socially connected all year long?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Second, what can we do to support caregivers within the Malay/Muslim community – especially those in the "sandwich generation" balancing work and parental care?

sections.label: Professional Networks for youth awareness
sections.summary: It asks how Professional Networks across over 10 industries can raise awareness of skills, careers and jobs for young people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: With the establishment of Professional Networks across over 10 industries, how can we leverage these networks to increase awareness about new skills, career pathways and job opportunities, especially for our young people?

sections.label: M3 FA4 career transition support
sections.summary: It states that under M3 Focus Area Four, unions and NTUC are ready to collaborate to strengthen structured career transition support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Under Focus Area Four (FA4) of M3, there is scope to strengthen support for this transition in a more structured manner.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The unions and the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) are ready to collaborate with MENDAKI, institutes of higher learning, employers and community partners, like MEMBINA Komuniti and 4PM, to enhance career guidance earlier on campus, provide channels to career coaching services and give advice on skills that are more targeted to growth sectors, expand access to industry mentors and professional networks, and lastly, open pathways, such as internships, place-and-train and entry-level roles in high-potential industries.

sections.label: Malay Heritage Centre reopening update
sections.summary: It asks the Minister for an update on programmes in the works and the Malay Heritage Centre reopening scheduled this April.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Could the Minister update us on the programmes in the works and the current status of the Malay Heritage Centre reopening, which is scheduled this April?

sections.label: M3 network collaboration
sections.summary: Asks how the M3 network can strengthen collaboration among MMOs, IMOs and partners through shared referrals and joint planning, and whether a common playbook will be considered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, how can the M3 network strengthen collaboration between MMOs, IMOs and other community partners, including shared referrals and joint planning, so individuals and families experience one coordinated pathway of help?

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Second, will the Minister consider a common playbook for MMOs, IMOs and partners with simple navigation standards and a small, shared set of outcomes, to make outreach more seamless.

sections.label: Three focus areas
sections.summary: States the speaker will focus on the SCIS, support for Malay/Indian and/or Muslim organisations, and social mobility for families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Chairman, I will focus on three areas – the SCIS, strengthening support for Malay/Indian and/or Muslim organisations, and increasing social mobility for our families.

sections.label: Standards for religious graduates
sections.summary: Asks to what extent targeted standards will emphasise religious understanding, spiritual capabilities and competencies of graduates guiding the Muslim community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Beyond academic qualifications, to what extent will the targeted standards emphasise strong religious understanding, comprehensive spiritual capabilities, as well as competencies of graduates guiding the Muslim community in facing current social challenges?

sections.label: CLF funds and Kurnia@WGS
sections.summary: Seeks a summary of CLF fund utilisation by MMOs/IMOs, new initiatives for uptake, and details on Kurnia@WGS achievements and expansion to other M3 towns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: At present, Yayasan MENDAKI has been working to ensure more can benefit from Community Leaders Forum (CLF) funds – a vital effort that must continue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I seek for a summary from the Acting Minister on the CLF fund utilisation rate by MMOs/IMOs and what new initiatives exist to encourage greater uptake.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Since January this year, it is understood that these two offices have been merged with M3@Geylang Serai to foster closer cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I hope the Acting Minister can share more about the achievements and future plans of Kurnia@WGS, and whether this effort will be expanded to other M3 towns, especially M3@Bedok under my purview.

sections.label: Support for vulnerable families
sections.summary: Asks the Acting Minister to summarise the support ecosystem's effectiveness for vulnerable families and share information and plans to enhance Project Dian.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Could the Acting Minister please summarise how effective this support ecosystem is for vulnerable families, and share the latest information as well as future plans to enhance Project Dian? : Chairman, good policy must translate in real life.

sections.label: Bersamamu marriage support
sections.summary: States that since its 2019 launch, Bersamamu has supported over 36,000 couples with marriage support and guidance from Kadi and Naib Kadi.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Since its launch in 2019, Bersamamu has supported over 36,000 couples, providing access to marriage support and guidance from our Kadi and Naib Kadi.

sections.label: Expanding Bersamamu marriage support
sections.summary: Bersamamu will expand with more Kadi and Naib Kadi, post-solemnisation sessions, mosque family development officers, and parenthood support.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To help more couples, like Mr Radzi and Ms Risa, we will be expanding the Bersamamu programme to further strengthen marriage support for Muslim couples.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will increase the pool of Kadi and Naib Kadi by about 50%, to better support newly wed Muslim couples, especially those who need more assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: These couples can benefit from additional post-solemnisation face-to-face sessions, to ensure they get a stronger start in their marriage journey.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will also make it easier for the community to access marriage support services, by deploying family development officers to selected mosques around Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Taken together, couples can get more help and targeted follow-up for those in higher-risk marriages, so that issues are addressed early before they escalate into crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will also expand the Bersamamu programme to include parenthood support, for more seamless assistance from marriage to parenthood.

sections.label: Project ARIF becomes permanent
sections.summary: About 5,000 couples benefited from the pilot, and Project ARIF becomes a permanent Bersamamu component from June 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Some 5,000 couples have benefited from the pilot and demonstrated improved maternal and child health outcomes, in terms of babies completing mandatory immunisations and being breastfed for at least three months.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Starting from June 2026, we will include Project ARIF as a permanent component under the Bersamamu programme.

sections.label: Pre-schoolers' Math Learning Support results
sections.summary: Nine in 10 participating pre-schoolers entered Primary 1 without requiring Learning Support for Math.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The results speak for themselves – nine in 10 participating pre-schoolers of this programme entered Primary 1 without requiring Learning Support for Math.

sections.label: MENDAKI mentoring starts earlier
sections.summary: MENDAKI's Youth Mentoring Office matched mentors to over 2,500 youths and will expand mentoring from Secondary 1.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Today, MENDAKI's Youth Mentoring Office has helped to match mentors to more than 2,500 youths, from Secondary 3 to undergraduates.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: MENDAKI will be expanding its mentoring programme to start earlier, from Secondary 1 students.

sections.label: MENDAKI and e2i AI readiness MOU
sections.summary: MENDAKI signed an MOU with NTUC's e2i to strengthen AI readiness through workshops and community engagement.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: MENDAKI has recently signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) to strengthen AI readiness through targeted workshops and community engagement initiatives.

sections.label: Programme expands to more mosques
sections.summary: With support from other mosques, the programme has expanded and benefits close to 900 seniors weekly.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The programme has since expanded with the support of other mosques, such as Masjid Darul Makmur and Masjid Yusof Ishak, benefiting close to 900 seniors weekly.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim seniors care programme
sections.summary: A targeted programme for Malay/Muslim seniors, developed by and for the community, will be supported by MUIS and PA.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This ecosystem of care affirmed the need for a targeted programme for our Malay/Muslim seniors that is developed by the community and for the community.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I have therefore asked MUIS and the People's Association (PA) to support Santunan Emas' efforts, and to help rally resources and agencies across health, social, financial and religious domains.

sections.label: AI business transformation schemes
sections.summary: Champions of AI, Enterprise Innovation Scheme enhancements and Productivity Solutions Grant expansion will help businesses transform and grow using AI.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Champions of AI programme, enhancements to the Enterprise Innovation Scheme and expansion of the Productivity Solutions Grant will be implemented to help businesses confidently transform and grow using AI.

sections.label: Langkah Digital AI upskilling
sections.summary: Langkah Digital, an M3 initiative by MENDAKI, offers workshops and events to strengthen AI and digital literacy in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As Minister of State Rahayu shared at the Ministry of Digital Development and Information's Committee of Supply (COS) debate, workers can upskill through Langkah Digital, an M3 initiative spearheaded by MENDAKI to strengthen AI and digital literacy amongst our community.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This will be done through practical workshops and events to help the community understand how best to make use of AI.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This will complement national measures announced by the Prime Minister, including the six months of free access to premium versions of AI tools, to help our community move from learning to applying AI and benefiting from it in their jobs.

sections.label: SCIS 2028 opening partnerships
sections.summary: SCIS remains on track to open in 2028, with an MOU signed with SUSS and partnerships being finalised in Egypt, Jordan and Morocco.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: SCIS remains on track to open in 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have signed an MOU with the Singapore University of Social Sciences, and we are finalising other partnerships with institutions in Egypt, Jordan and Morocco.

sections.label: WMS fundraising total
sections.summary: As of February 2026, the WMS has raised over $8.5 million from over 15,400 transactions.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As of February 2026, the WMS has raised over $8.5 million, with contributions from over 15,400 transactions.

sections.label: MHC reopening festival
sections.summary: The MHC will reopen in April with Pesta Pecah Panggung, featuring programmes by over 60 partners.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The MHC will reopen in April this year with Pesta Pecah Panggung – Transcending Boundaries, a festival featuring programmes by over 60 partners showcasing the best of Singapore and Nusantara arts, youth talent and community creativity.

sections.label: MHC research unit
sections.summary: The MHC will establish a research unit led by an advisory panel chaired by Dr Norshahril Saat to build knowledge about Singapore Malay heritage.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The MHC will establish a research unit led by an advisory panel with Dr Norshahril Saat as the chair to build a comprehensive body of knowledge about Singapore Malay heritage.

sections.label: Intangible Cultural Heritage Mentorship Programme
sections.summary: The MHC launched an Intangible Cultural Heritage Mentorship Programme connecting experienced practitioners with young enthusiasts over a 10-week structured programme.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The MHC has also launched an Intangible Cultural Heritage Mentorship Programme, connecting experienced practitioners with young enthusiasts over a 10-week structured programme.

sections.label: Expanding and rebranding M3
sections.summary: To broaden collaborative networks, M3 will be expanded and rebranded to M3+.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: However, as Dr Hamid Razak and Ms Hazlina Halim have pointed out, we must broaden our collaborative networks to achieve these goals.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will therefore expand and rebrand M3 to M3+.

sections.label: MENDAKI fund and Project DIAN
sections.summary: In 2025 MENDAKI disbursed over $2 million from the Community Leaders' Forum Fund, and Project DIAN reached over 900 families as at end 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For instance, in 2025, MENDAKI disbursed more than $2 million from the Community Leaders' Forum Fund, which Ms Hazlina spoke about.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: It is important that we facilitate collaboration and improve coordination by bringing together M3 agencies and our community partners to develop better ways of working together.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This includes ongoing efforts under Project DIAN, where we have reached out to over 900 families as at end 2025.

sections.label: Bersamamu and Project ARIF
sections.summary: Bersamamu, which has supported over 36,000 couples, will be enhanced, and Project ARIF will become a permanent programme.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Bersamamu programme has supported over 36,000 couples, will be enhanced by increasing the pool of Kadi and Naib Kadi by about 50%, and deploying Family Development Officers to selected mosques.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In addition, Project ARIF will become a permanent programme to help couples throughout their journey from marriage to parenthood.

sections.label: Mosques as community hubs
sections.summary: Mosques will continue as dynamic community hubs, and an MOU with SUSS was signed to offer an inter-disciplinary undergraduate curriculum.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Mosques will continue to play a key role as dynamic community hubs to strengthen community bonds, address social needs and meet the needs of religious life that is constantly evolving.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have signed an MOU with SUSS to offer an inter-disciplinary curriculum for undergraduate programmes.

sections.label: Malay Heritage Centre reopening
sections.summary: The Malay Heritage Centre will reopen in April this year.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Malay Heritage Centre will reopen in April this year.

sections.label: M3+ network launch
sections.summary: A network will be launched in April 2026, starting with an M3+ networking session, to explore opportunities for more effective coordination.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: They will explore new opportunities where efforts can be coordinated more effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This network will be launched in April 2026, starting with an M3+ networking session.

sections.label: Community vision and three pillars
sections.summary: The speaker shared a vision of a thriving community and outlined three pillars addressing every dimension of community development.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I have shared my vision for our community, to cultivate a thriving community where every member can be the best version of themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I have outlined how we will achieve this vision through three pillars that address every dimension of our community's development.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Through these three pillars, we ensure that every member of our community can build secure and prosperous futures while remaining grounded in the values and rich culture that define us as a community.

sections.label: Strengthening support and collective spirit
sections.summary: Support will be strengthened by building capable, trusted institutions and engaging closely, with strength lying in collective spirit.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As we move forward, we will continue strengthening support by building capable, trusted institutions and more importantly, by engaging one another closely on issues that are close to our hearts.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Our true strength lies in our collective spirit, the same spirit that sees neighbours helping neighbours, organisations collaborating across boundaries and leaders emerging to serve the greater good.

sections.label: Haj 2026 preparations
sections.summary: There is close contact with Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Hajj and Umrah, Haj 2026 preparations continue uninterrupted, and pilgrim safety is the utmost priority.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For Haj, as at today, we are in close contact with Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Hajj and Umrah.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: To-date, all preparation for the Haj 2026 season continues uninterrupted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Above all, the safety of our pilgrims remains our utmost priority.

sections.label: Malay community success and research unit
sections.summary: The Malay community can continue to strive for success while keeping its tradition and identity, and a research unit is being set up.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And that has enabled the Malay community here to be able to continue, while keeping to its tradition and identity, to strive for success and excel in their life.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We are also setting up the research unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: I was wondering if the Minister can share a bit more, whether we can enhance and increase the budget and resources for MENDAKI, so that these efforts can be increased, especially when the Government, in this year's Budget, has been talking about AI Missions and AI Champions.

sections.label: MUIS and PA MESRA outreach

sentences.text: I see it as a very good platform for us to extend our outreach.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Therefore, as I mentioned, I have instructed MUIS and PA MESRA to look at how we can support this effort so that we can reach out to more members of our community and help them age gracefully.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So I agree with what Mr Saktiandi said earlier, and we will expand this approach.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: All these clarifications, let us push it to the back, at the end of the rest of the cuts.

sections.label: Multiculturalism as Singapore identity anchor

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this context, I welcome MCCY's clear decision to position multiculturalism as an anchor of our Singapore identity.

sections.label: Sports benefits and CCA access
sections.summary: A Member says sports build resilience, teamwork, discipline and healthy habits, but students find joining CCAs difficult without aptitude.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Chairman, beyond competition and medals, sports build resilience, teamwork, discipline and healthy habits for young people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: However, many students today find it difficult to join school co-curricular activities (CCAs) unless they already demonstrate a certain level of aptitude.

sections.label: SpexSG company limited by guarantee
sections.summary: From 1 April, the company limited by guarantee called SpexSG will be in effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: From 1 April, the company limited by guarantee called SpexSG will be in effect.

sections.label: Consolidation benefits timeline
sections.summary: Benefits of the consolidation are expected to take a year or two to be fully reaped.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: It is things that have already been going on.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: But we do expect to take the better of the next year or two before we can fully reap a lot of the benefits of the consolidation that I talked about earlier.

sections.label: SG Partnerships Fund questions
sections.summary: An MP asks about Sprout tier co-funding, tax deduction, funding flexibility and MCCY support for fundraising.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
sentences.text: My final question has to do with the SG Partnerships Fund.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
sentences.text: It was mentioned that for the Sprout tier, there is a 20% co-funding requirement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
sentences.text: I was wondering if the Minister could elaborate on whether donations would qualify for the 250% tax deduction or whether this could be funded through earned revenue, whether there is flexibility in how this contribution could be structured and whether MCCY could provide support to help organisations or to help these initiatives secure these funds, particularly in the area of fundraising and partnership development.

sections.label: MCCY as NSA conduit
sections.summary: MCCY commits to being the Government conduit for NSAs working with MOE on DSA criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: On the second question about the DSA criteria, whether MCCY can help the NSAs work more closely with MOE – when I meet up with all the NSA presidents and vice presidents, my commitment to all the NSAs is that MCCY will be the Government conduit.

sections.label: Sprout and Scale tier funding
sections.summary: Sprout tier is $50,000 over two years and Scale tier $1 million over three years, with co-funding from donations or earned revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For the Sprout tier, it is $50,000 over two years, and for the Scale tier, it is $1 million over three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Allow me to assure him that the 20% to be co-funded does not have to be done upfront.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And the source of funding that he mentioned, whether is it donation or earned revenue, they are allowable.

sections.label: OBS priority for MOE
sections.summary: The priority for OBS is the MOE-OBS Challenge scale-up for Secondary 3 students up to 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my main speech, our priority for OBS is the MOE-OBS Challenge scale-up for Secondary 3 students up to 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: That will be our priority – to get it right, to make sure we do it well.

sections.label: Woodlands adjustable weights trial
sections.summary: A Woodlands trial is looking at adjustable weights for outdoor machines, to be rolled out when data supports it.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: For example, there is a trial in Woodlands, if I am not wrong, where we are also looking at adjustable weights for outdoor machines.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: These are all things we are looking at and when we have sufficient data and confidence that some of these things work well in an outdoor setting, we will proceed to roll them out.

sections.label: After-dark programmes and NYC role
sections.summary: The speaker says they are keen to study and pilot possible after-dark programmes, including in museums, and NYC will have a big role.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: Well, we will certainly be very keen to study as well as pilot possible programmes after dark, whether it is in our museums or otherwise, and certainly NYC will have a big role to play in this.

sections.label: Place-making Project Office coverage
sections.summary: The new Place-making Project Office under the Inter-agency Task Force serves Kampong Gelam, Little India and also Chinatown.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: As far as his historic district is concerned, I want to assure him that the new Place-making Project Office that comes under the Inter-agency Task Force does indeed not only serve Kampong Gelam, Little India, but also Chinatown.

sections.label: MOE-OBS Challenge sites
sections.summary: The MOE-OBS Challenge will primarily use OBS' sites, namely Pulau Ubin and the upcoming Coney Island campus.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: To the Member's questions on sites for the MOE-OBS Challenge, yes, it will primarily be OBS' sites, so, they will be Pulau Ubin and also the Coney Island campus that will be coming up.
